A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same shard-sharing PEFT work, renamed from FOSSIL, with older Bone/DiSHA appendix labels, to MiSS. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v9 reports original synthetic adaptation experiments, GLUE and math/code evaluations, convergence and resource measurements, and RWKV7 results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v11 retains original benchmark and appendix results and adds a broad Llama-3.2-3B PEFT comparison and expanded gradient-norm measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the zero-initialized shared matrix D, shard expansion, and efficient block-summation formulation in Section 4 and equations 2–6. The renaming and changed illustrative pseudocode do not establish a new procedure; both explicit expansion and efficient aggregation were already described in v9.

E1.justification: The identifiable coverage—synthetic sinusoidal adaptation, five GLUE tasks, MetaMathQA, CodeFeedback, GSM8K, Math, HumanEval and MBPP—is retained. v11 does not identify the dataset or task behind its new Llama-3.2-3B comparison in Table 6, so it is unclear whether this expands data/task coverage or only changes model and evaluation settings.

E2.justification: v11 Table 6 substantially expands evaluated comparators, including RSLORA, C3A, RANDLORA, SHIRA, OFT, LoRA-FA and multiple prompt/adaptation methods absent from v9's reported comparisons. Comparator membership in the retained GLUE, math/code and RWKV7 tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v11 adds a Llama-3.2-3B benchmarking protocol reporting total/train time, test accuracy, training loss, and maximum, 99th-percentile reserved and average reserved memory. It removes v9's RWKV6 throughput evaluation on one and four RTX 4090 GPUs. The shared NLU/NLG and synthetic settings remain unchanged; these are added and removed evaluations, not established reruns under revised settings.

E4.justification: The initial-gradient-versus-rank diagnostic expands from v9 Figure 4's single panel to four panels covering LLaMA2-7B and Qwen3-4B on math and code in v11 Figure 1. The separate LoRA/PiSSA/FOSSIL loss-versus-step comparison disappears. The task-score rank ablation and LoRA-versus-proposed-method loss/token and loss/time comparisons remain.

E5.justification: v11 removes the checklist's blanket assurance that all experiments were repeated and averaged. Explicit reporting otherwise remains: GLUE uses three seeds and ± entries, Appendix B specifies seed 43, and the NLG three-run caption still conflicts with the two-seed prose. The new Table 6 supplies no run counts or uncertainty estimates; fewer actual runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports MiSS accuracy of 0.5080 versus LoRA's 0.4822 and RSLORA's 0.5299, alongside extensive resource results. v9's RWKV6 resource results are removed and gradient-norm results are expanded/replaced. Tables 2–4 and the RWKV7 scores remain numerically unchanged. v11 Section 5.2 newly misattributes 8.58 to HumanEval; both Table 3s identify it as Math, with HumanEval at 23.63.

T1.justification: The low-rank argument, expansion definition, aggregation equations and asymptotic complexity expressions are retained, including v9 Figure 5's complexity display becoming v11 Table 5. The new optimization explanation adds no formal assumptions, theorem, proof or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v9 primarily presents shard sharing as a favorable adaptability–efficiency trade-off. v11 makes simultaneous optimization of LoRA's A and B a central cause of slow convergence and claims that updating one matrix reduces optimization complexity without compromising performance. This substantially changes the explanatory claim in the abstract, introduction and conclusion, although the underlying method is retained.

C2.justification: v11 interprets larger gradient norms as support for simpler single-matrix optimization and describes its new Pareto results as uniquely optimal. Section 5.3 replaces v9's hypothesis about small-rank generalization failure with a recommendation for rank 64. Section 7 also removes the explicit acknowledgment that hardware constraints prevented full-scale training.

D1.justification: v11 changes the advertised project repository, rewrites the implementation snippet and identifies the PEFT benchmarking framework. It drops the removed RWKV6 experiment's batch-size, context-length, GPU and checkpointing disclosures. The NLG and synthetic hyperparameter tables are otherwise retained. The PDFs do not establish the contents or availability of the changed repository.

R1.justification: v11 adds citations to S2FT, StableMask and the PEFT software. S2FT now helps motivate the single-matrix optimization argument, and the introduction adds specific criticisms of prior approaches. The existing LoRA-variant survey and most research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages, results discussion, rank discussion and conclusion are rewritten. Gradient analysis moves into the introduction, the resource subsection is replaced by a Pareto subsection, terminology is consolidated under MiSS, and the lengthy NeurIPS checklist is removed. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The method schematic is redrawn and relocated, the synthetic plots are restyled, gradient norms become four panels, and the loss plots are resized and reformatted. New Pareto panels and a dense comparison table replace the earlier resource display. The complexity display and appendix tables are retained with changed labeling, numbering and layout.

improvement.justification: v11 adds comparison breadth, broader gradient diagnostics and more consistent terminology. However, Table 6 leaves its dataset and key settings unspecified, while Section 5.4 claims optimality despite RSLORA's higher accuracy and LoRA-FA's lower memory. The revision also removes an explicit hardware limitation and introduces the Math/HumanEval attribution error. These evidential and presentation gains coexist with reporting and interpretation harms, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
